title: Value of napsin A and thyroid transcription factor-1 in the identification of primary lung adenocarcinoma
text: In a cohort containing primary lung cancers and metastases, Napsin A and TTF-1 were frequently expressed in primary lung adenocarcinoma. The study also observed TTF-1 expression outside lung adenocarcinoma, supporting interpretation as a panel rather than as an isolated marker.

title: Various antibody clones of Napsin A, TTF-1, and p40 in non-small cell lung carcinoma
text: This tissue-microarray study evaluated CK5, p63, and p40 as squamous markers and Napsin A and TTF-1 as lung adenocarcinoma markers. Reported performance varied by marker and antibody clone, and combining Napsin A with TTF-1 improved sensitivity.

title: Immunostaining for TTF-1, Napsin A, p40, and cytokeratin 5 aids differential diagnosis of NSCLC
text: The study compared marker combinations for separating lung adenocarcinoma from squamous cell carcinoma. TTF-1 and Napsin A supported adenocarcinoma, while p40 and CK5 supported squamous differentiation; the combined panel was more informative than a single stain.

title: Decision tree for pulmonary adenocarcinoma with mucinous features versus metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma
text: A decision tree using TTF-1, SATB2, CDX2, and CK7 was developed to distinguish primary pulmonary adenocarcinoma with mucinous features from metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma. The validation results support using multiple markers and clinical context when assigning a primary site.

title: HNF4-alpha and SATB2 in pulmonary and colorectal adenocarcinomas
text: In a large immunohistochemical series, Napsin A and TTF-1 were much more frequent in pulmonary adenocarcinoma, whereas CDX2, CK20, HNF4-alpha, and SATB2 were much more frequent in colorectal metastases. Rare cross-expression occurred, so no individual marker was absolute.

title: A vision-language foundation model for precision oncology
text: MUSK is a vision-language foundation model trained on pathology images and pathology-related text. The published evaluations include cross-modal retrieval, visual question answering, image classification, and several outcome-prediction tasks. Its output remains task- and dataset-dependent and requires downstream validation.

title: Histologic features of herpes simplex virus esophagitis
text: HSV esophagitis can show ulceration, necrotic debris, multinucleated giant squamous cells, ground-glass or eosinophilic intranuclear inclusions, nuclear molding, and chromatin margination. Viral immunohistochemistry or another confirmatory method may be needed because viral esophagitis patterns can overlap.

title: Histologic features of cytomegalovirus esophagitis
text: CMV cytopathic effect is typically found in endothelial and stromal cells at the ulcer base. Histology may show cytomegaly, eccentrically positioned basophilic intranuclear inclusions surrounded by a clear halo, pale perinuclear regions, and an owl-eye appearance; CMV immunohistochemistry can confirm infected cells.

title: Histologic features of Candida esophagitis
text: Candida esophagitis shows fungal hyphae, pseudohyphae, and spores along or invading squamous epithelium, often with neutrophilic inflammation, erosion, ulceration, and necrotic debris. PAS or Grocott methenamine silver stains help demonstrate fungal forms and distinguish Candida from viral esophagitis.

title: Sampling and confirmation in infectious esophagitis
text: For suspected HSV esophagitis, diagnostic cytopathic changes are most likely at the ulcer edge and in sloughed squamous cells. Candida requires demonstration of pseudohyphae or true hyphae and assessment of tissue invasion rather than isolated budding yeasts in exudate. Histology may require organism-specific immunostaining, in situ hybridization, culture, or special stains for confirmation.

title: Pulmonary adenocarcinoma histology
text: Pulmonary adenocarcinoma can show lepidic, acinar, papillary, micropapillary, or solid growth with mucin, and mixed patterns are common. Squamous differentiation is supported morphologically by keratinization, keratin pearl formation, and intercellular bridges. Poorly differentiated tumors may require immunohistochemistry.

title: Colorectal carcinoma: pathologic aspects
text: Colorectal adenocarcinoma commonly forms malignant glands. Invasion can be accompanied by desmoplastic stroma, and glandular lumina frequently contain characteristic dirty necrosis. Benign colonic mucosa retains orderly crypt architecture and mature goblet cells without dysplasia.

title: Educational case: basal cell carcinoma and its histologic differential
text: Basal cell carcinoma shows dermal islands of basophilic tumor cells with peripheral nuclear palisading, stromal retraction, and loose mucinous stroma. Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma shows invasive islands of pleomorphic keratinocytes arising from the epidermis with prominent nucleoli and increased mitoses. Melanoma can show irregular nests and single pleomorphic pigmented melanocytes within the epidermis and dermis.
